summary: German linking words come in three groups, and each group does something different to the word order. (1) und, oder, aber, denn (and sondern) stand between two main clauses and change nothing: Ich bin müde, aber ich gehe zur Arbeit. (2) Adverbs such as deshalb, deswegen, also, dann (and trotzdem) take the first place of their clause, so the verb follows at once: Ich habe Hunger, deshalb esse ich ein Brot. (3) Subordinating conjunctions – weil, dass, wenn, als, ob, obwohl – send the conjugated verb to the END of their clause: …, weil ich Durst habe. If the subordinate clause comes first, it fills the first place of the sentence and the main clause starts with its verb: Weil es kalt ist, trinken wir Tee (verb – comma – verb). A comma always separates the clauses. A separable verb joins up again at the end (…, weil der Zug um acht ankommt) and a modal verb comes last (…, weil ich Tee trinken will). Three English words split in German: “because” is weil (verb last) or denn (normal order); “when” is wenn (present, future, every time), als (one event in the past) or the question word wann; “if” is wenn (a condition) or ob (whether).

blocks.title: Spoken “weil” with normal order
blocks.text: In fast speech you will hear weil ich habe Durst. It is common colloquially but wrong in writing: weil ich Durst habe.

blocks.title: also is a false friend
blocks.text: German also = so, therefore. English “also” is auch: Ich komme auch (I’m coming too).

blocks.title: das or dass?
blocks.text: If you can say dieses or welches instead, write das (article / pronoun); otherwise it is the conjunction dass.

blocks.title: Ask yourself when you join two clauses
questions: Which group is the linking word in: und / oder / aber / denn, deshalb / also / dann, or weil / dass / wenn / als / ob / obwohl?
Group 1 → keep the normal order. Group 2 → verb right after it. Group 3 → verb to the end.
Does the subordinate clause come first? → the main clause starts with its verb.

traps: weil sends the verb to the end: weil ich müde bin (not *weil ich bin müde in writing).
denn keeps normal order and never starts a sentence: Warum? – Weil … (not *Denn …).
deshalb / also / dann + verb next: deshalb esse ich (not *deshalb ich esse).
Subordinate clause first → the main clause starts with the verb: Wenn es kalt ist, bleiben wir zu Hause.
als for one event in the past, wenn for present / future / repeated, wann for questions.
if = whether → ob; if = condition → wenn.
A comma before weil, dass, wenn, ob, obwohl, aber, denn.

quiz.q: Ich trinke Wasser, weil ich Durst ___.
quiz.why: After weil the verb goes to the end – and it is still conjugated (ich habe).

options: Ich habe Hunger, deshalb esse ich.
Ich habe Hunger, deshalb ich esse.
Ich habe Hunger, deshalb ich esse jetzt.
quiz.answer: Ich habe Hunger, deshalb esse ich.
quiz.why: deshalb takes the first place; the verb follows at once.

options: Ich trinke Wasser, denn ich habe Durst.
Ich trinke Wasser, denn ich Durst habe.
Ich trinke Wasser, denn habe ich Durst.
quiz.answer: Ich trinke Wasser, denn ich habe Durst.

quiz.q: ___ mein Opa jung war, war er Bauer.
quiz.why: One period in the past → als.

quiz.q: ___ es kalt ist, trinken wir Tee. (every time)
Ich weiß nicht, ___ er heute kommt.

quiz.why: The weil-clause fills the first place → the main clause starts with its verb.

quiz.q: Wir gehen in den Park, ___ es kalt ist. (although)
quiz.why: obwohl + verb at the end; trotzdem is an adverb (…, trotzdem gehen wir).

seeAlso.note: Arabic: لٰكِنَّ (but), لِأَنَّ (because) and أَنَّ (that) take a noun in the accusative or a suffix (لِأَنَّهُ …); لِذٰلِكَ (therefore), عِنْدَمَا (when), إِذَا (if). The word order inside the clause does not change.
Hebrew: אֲבָל (but), כִּי (because), לָכֵן (therefore), שֶׁ (that) written onto the next word, כְּשֶׁ (when), אִם (if), אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁ (although) – no change of word order.
Chinese uses pairs: 因为 … 所以 … (because … so …), 虽然 … 但是 … (although … but …), 如果 …(的话) … 就 … (if … then …), and …的时候 (when …) before the main clause – no verb movement.
wann (when?) is the question word of S10; wenn and als are the linking words.
The verb-first order of a yes/no question (Bleibst du zu Hause?) stays the same when a weil-clause follows: Bleibst du zu Hause, weil du müde bist?
